title: Nilpotent Faber–Krahn and Weyl asymptotic nodal-domain bound for closed equiregular sub-Riemannian manifolds
source_title: On Courant and Pleijel theorems for sub-Riemannian Laplacians
author: Rupert L. Frank; Bernard Helffer
difficulty_reason: Nilpotent pointwise models do not directly control small nodal domains uniformly across a varying sub-Riemannian manifold. The authors establish uniform energy comparison and continuity of the local Faber–Krahn constants, then use a controlled IMS partition to obtain a small-volume inequality involving their integrated density rather than a coarse infimum. Together with the new Sobolev nodal restriction, that local-to-global estimate supplies the nonroutine part of the nodal count beyond the precise prior kernel/Weyl foundations.

Theorem4.1 gives the stated integrated nilpotent Faber–Krahn/Weyl bound; strict inequality below one is not asserted unconditionally. Full local operator comparison22–24, nilpotent positivity and continuity24–27, small-set IMS argument27–29, nodal summation29–30 and frame reduction69–71 read. Definitions and nodal restriction10–19 read. The low homogeneous-dimension extension is explicitly supplied by product and scaling on25. Published Metivier and Rothschild–Stein operator and Weyl results are identified background, not missing new cores. No Heisenberg numerical variant selected.

historical_source_pdf_evidence.original_difficulty_reason: The authors establish a uniform local comparison with nilpotentized operators, continuity of optimal Faber–Krahn constants, and a small-domain IMS inequality, then derive the integrated asymptotic nodal bound. These novel subelliptic spectral constructions exceed qualifying-exam analysis.
